name: Benign-only detector on real production web logs (Zenodo 20001206, two Indonesian public-sector organizations)
registered: 2026-11-27, after reading only archive member names and sizes, per-file line counts, date ranges, counts of requests with a query string, log line shapes with letters and digits masked, and the publisher's YAML labeling rules; before any request path or query value was read and before any model was fitted
question: On real users' traffic, how many alerts does the detector raise, and how many of them have independent evidence of an attack?

source.dataset: Web Server Log Dataset, Zenodo 20001206, MIT

scope: Access-log requests whose target has a query string: Organization X web-access.log*, Organization Y per-site home/<site>/logs/*.access_log*. Server-level logs under usr/local are excluded because they repeat per-site requests. Requests without a query string carry no input values and are out of scope for this detector.
mapping: template = site + method + path with each run of digits replaced by 9; inputs = URL-decoded query values (parse_qsl, keep blanks, decoding errors replaced) joined by single spaces.
split: By time, per organization, in the log's own time zone offset: Organization X trains on requests before 2025-10-01 00:00 +07:00 and is tested from then on; Organization Y trains before 2025-04-22 00:00 +07:00 and is tested from then on, a period that includes the reported incident of 2025-04-29.
training_contamination: Training uses every in-scope request in the training period, unlabeled, as a deployment would. Real traffic contains attacks, so profiles may absorb some; this is reported, not removed.
method: The v3 SQL method (input novelty per template: character classes and length; tail probabilities on a benign calibration split; Fisher fusion; 40/35/25 split; threshold at 0.5%; seed 2026112801) with one registered adaptation for scale: the isolation forest's template one-hot (thousands of templates on real sites) is replaced by one feature, log(1 + training count of the template), 0 when unseen. No other change and no tuning on these logs. One model per organization.
independent_evidence: Each test request is also judged by: OWASP CRS paranoia levels 1 and 2 (owasp/modsecurity-crs:nginx, digest recorded, browser headers, the original target replayed as a GET), and libinjection 1.1.6 SQL injection and XSS checks on each input value. A request has independent evidence of attack if any of these flags it. The publisher's YAML rules are not used as labels: they match on user agents and status codes and do not inspect inputs.
measures: Alert rate at the frozen threshold over in-scope test requests, overall, per organization, per site, per day, and split by seen and unseen templates; alerts per day; share of alerts with independent evidence; alert rate among requests with independent evidence (a detection proxy); the same for each component alone.
pass_condition: Per organization: alerts without independent evidence are at most 1% of in-scope test requests. Headline: organizations passing out of 2.
review_sample: 200 alerts without independent evidence per organization, drawn with seed 2026112702, are kept as a workflow artifact with client addresses removed, for human review. They are not committed, because query values can hold personal data of the sites' users. The committed report holds counts only.
known_limits: Neither the alerts nor the misses are confirmed by hand in this run. CRS and libinjection have their own errors. Training data is unlabeled real traffic. POST bodies are not logged, so only query strings are seen.
not_claimed: A confirmed false-alarm rate; detection of attacks that leave no trace in query strings.
